corrected_adjudication.reasoning: Attempt 2 completed all parent calls and left every observed mutation boundary clean, but it is not selectable. One nested canary recovered from a provider overload, the reviewed canary contract incorrectly prohibited TaskTool's mandatory terminal yield, unrestricted user-profile discovery widened all six child surfaces with ambient MCP tools, and a parser exception was incorrectly promoted to an environment block by scanning unrelated historical transcript text. These are sample-integrity and harness defects, not evidence for or against the isolation-apply semantics.

root_cause_source_evidence.finding: TaskTool sets requireYieldTool=true, ordinary explicit child surfaces gain hub, and yielded data determines finalized task output.
The registry includes yield when the caller requires it.
Yield is force-included into an explicit list when required, while unrestricted custom and extension-registered tools widen the active surface.
External user-level discovery paths resolve from the load context home, not only from the native agent directory.
User configuration bases are rooted at os.homedir(), including .codex and other external tool homes.
The yield tool validates and submits structured terminal results; it is an execution protocol, not a passive surface entry.

regression_corrections: Empty PSCustomObject property enumeration is valid and deterministic under StrictMode.
Capture failures can no longer scan transcript text to invent provider/environment provenance.
Canary task prompts and agent instructions require one exact terminal yield and forbid every other tool call.
Canary result parsing accepts only the exact acknowledgement object and rejects prose or widened objects.
Canary session parsing requires exact [read, yield, hub], deduplicates message/execution records by tool-call ID, and exposes all forbidden calls.
Recovered non-terminal nested provider errors invalidate an attempt before semantic classification.
The runner creates a disposable user profile, injects USERPROFILE only into the child process, and redacts that path in durable run metadata.
The E3-I phase contract, cross-cutting isolation contract, design, plan, fixture agent, and prompts now describe the same terminal-yield-only protocol.

provider_execution.note: The nested runtime's recovered provider request is recorded as sample contamination, not as a Codex-authorized experiment retry.

non_claims: Attempt 2 provides no selected I1, I2, I3, or I4 PASS evidence.
The apparent project/runtime branch split is not selectable because the canary protocol, capability boundary, and retry-free sample requirement were violated.
Session B was not launched and no Attempt 2 observation may be combined with a later selected attempt.
E3-I remains diagnostic evidence only and does not gate or authorize parallel execution.
This adjudication does not claim that ambient MCP discovery is a product defect; it is an experiment-isolation defect for this controlled canary.
